tasks.redPrompt:
RED for #259 (rules: _shared of teams/mvox-dev/memory/pipeline-args/args-259.json — read it first). Surgical guard on three awaits; the page's own idiom supplies the mechanism.

VERIFIED FACTS (research @ a8d5ba2 — re-grep): the three unguarded inactiveRows writes are roster/+page.svelte handleDeactivateConfirm (:809), toggleInactive (:845), handleReinstate (:874) — each awaits loadInactiveRoster(cfg) with cfg captured earlier and assigns with no generation check. Post-#232 the page runs on createRouteLoadMachine whose header comment DOCUMENTS the external co-guard seam: machine.generation (non-mutating getter) + machine.isCurrent(g); the page already uses `const g = routeLoad.generation; … if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` four times for structural-write reconciles. The #255 panel-reset (isSwitch-gated clear citing '#255 review r3 F2') is intact; a stale write while the panel is closed silently repopulates inactiveRows and the next open on collective B renders A's rows with live Reinstate buttons.

THE TRAP (research-proven, pin it): loadForSelected() BUMPS the generation unconditionally (`const g = ++generation`). handleDeactivateConfirm and handleReinstate each call `await loadForSelected()` BEFORE their inactiveRows reload — so the guard generation must be captured AFTER each function's own loadForSelected() call, NOT at function entry; entry-capture would make isCurrent(g) false on EVERY ordinary deactivate/reinstate-with-panel-open and silently skip the reload (stale panel on the non-race path — worse than the bug). toggleInactive does not call loadForSelected, so entry-capture is correct there. RED must pin BOTH halves: (i) the race — mock loadInactiveRoster with a test-held deferred (the file's existing release-controlled mock pattern, cf. the 'second tap while reinstate in flight' test), open the panel, start the load, SWITCH collectives mid-flight, then settle the stale promise → assert inactiveRows/DOM does NOT show collective A's rows (deterministic hold→switch→settle construction; per the house race-proof method the failure must trip on the panel content assertion, not a timeout, and the RED report carries the verbatim pre-fix failure output); (ii) the non-race path — ordinary deactivate and reinstate with the panel open still refresh it (guards mis-captured at entry would fail THESE — they are the trap detectors). All existing page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts blocks (incl. 'switching collectives clears the panel' — a post-settle switch, different case) must stay green UNTOUCHED.

Scope fence: memberLifecycle.ts untouched; routeLoad.ts untouched (the seam already exists); no store/API changes; #255 reset semantics untouched.

tasks.commitBody:
The roster's inactive-panel loads raced a collective switch: three
awaits (panel open, post-deactivate refresh, post-reinstate
refresh) wrote inactiveRows with no generation check, so collective
A's in-flight load could settle after a switch to B and repopulate
the panel with A's members — live Reinstate buttons aimed at
foreign ids. Filed from #255's round-4 review as the converging
tail of that chain; merged then because the render self-heals and
no cross-collective write is possible, fixed now.

The guard is the page's own idiom: the #232 route-load machine's
documented external co-guard seam (generation captured without
bumping, compared at settle — the same shape as its four existing
structural-write reconciles and #260's completion-gate guard). A
stale settle writes nothing, rows nor error.

The capture points are deliberately per-site, and the tests pin
why: loadForSelected bumps the generation, so the two lifecycle
sites capture AFTER their own loadForSelected call — an
entry-capture would silently skip the panel refresh on every
ordinary deactivate and reinstate, trading a rare race for a
broken normal path. The non-race refresh tests exist precisely to
catch that mis-capture.

The race test is deterministically ordered (held promise → switch
→ settle) and its pre-fix failure output — the panel showing the
left collective's rows — is in the review record, per the house
standard for timing proofs.

Live gate (Mihkel): with two collectives, open the roster's
inactive panel in A, switch to B while it loads — B never shows
A's inactive members; deactivating with the panel open still
refreshes it.
